## Why

This is the screen everyday users actually use. It must be readable at a glance and need one tap at most. S62 serves a placeholder at `/` for paired devices; this slice replaces its body and keeps the URL and the `home.index` endpoint.

## Owner input

None. Owner decisions: 2026-11-04 (ADR 0013 Rules, S19): a skipped meal rolls to the next open night, so the Today view's skip control moves the meal there. 2026-11-05, answered by the owner: (1) the view shows tonight's dinner only, with a 'view recipe' link to the read-only recipe page (S14); tomorrow's dinner and a defrost hint are not built; (2) the buttons read 'Made it' and 'Skip tonight'.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-05, spec-check answers: (1) the shopping-list link points at the fixed path /list now; it 404s until S25 serves /list, and S25 must register that path; (2) when 'Skip tonight' finds no open night left in the same Sunday-start week, tonight is marked skipped, nothing is created and the user is told there was no night to move it to (no cross-week writes); (3) after 'Made it' or 'Skip tonight' the page shows a confirmation state, the meal as made or as skipped and moved to a named night, instead of the planned-meal controls.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-05, spec-check answer: 'Made it' and 'Skip tonight' write only the planned_meal status and do not fire plan_confirmed; the shopping list keeps its plan items until the next confirmed plan save, so items a shopper already ticked are not un-checked. Any further small implementation detail this spec does not cover is the implementer's call within the decisions above; list each such choice in the report's deviations so the owner can review it.
